comments.note: scripts/kill-orchestrator.js: The findRecentPlanDirs() function uses fs.statSync() inside a try/catch to determine if a plan path is a file vs directory. This silently ignores paths where plan files no longer exist on disk. A minor note comment in the code would clarify this is intentional.

scripts/kill-orchestrator.js: Lock cleanup scans the last 20 logs. For workspaces with very active orchestrator usage (many consecutive runs), plan dirs from >20 runs ago won't be scanned. Could be configurable, but 20 is a reasonable default for the current use case.

scripts/kill-orchestrator.js: The 3-second SIGTERM wait is hardcoded. For orchestrator processes that are deep in an LLM API call, 3 seconds may not be sufficient for a graceful shutdown. SIGKILL fallback is safe but could interrupt in-flight work. Low priority since the script is for stale/stuck processes.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (scripts/kill-orchestrator.js, scripts/cli.js). 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (path traversal concern — bounded impact, noted below). 2 Low. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01/A08 — Path Traversal (bounded): scripts/kill-orchestrator.js findRecentPlanDirs() (line ~220). The `entry.plan` value read from JSONL log files is used directly to construct a filesystem path without validating it stays within the workspace root. A maliciously crafted JSONL log entry with plan: '/arbitrary/path' would cause cleanupStaleLocks() to attempt fs.rmSync('/arbitrary/path/.orchestrator.lock'). Impact is bounded: (1) the appended filename is always the hard-coded '.orchestrator.lock', so only files with that exact name can be deleted; (2) exploitation requires write access to orchestrator/logs/, which presupposes local filesystem access. Defence-in-depth recommendation: add a guard `if (!path.resolve(planDir).startsWith(WORKSPACE_ROOT)) continue;` before adding to planDirs, to unconditionally constrain cleanup to workspace directories.

A03 — Injection: confirmed safe. spawnSync calls for pgrep, ps, and process.kill all use shell: false (or syscall directly). PID values are validated via parseInt+isNaN before use. cmdline from pgrep is only sent to console.log after slicing to 120 chars — never used in shell invocations. No injection surface identified.

A06 — Dependencies: scripts/kill-orchestrator.js has zero external dependencies (Node.js stdlib only: fs, path, child_process, readline). No CVE exposure from new packages. cli.js changes are limited to adding a single command registration entry with no new dependencies. Dependency audit: PASS.

summary: PASS — implementation is clean, well-architected, and follows all workspace patterns. One Fix-Forward correction applied.

Fix: Applied the path traversal defence-in-depth guard in findRecentPlanDirs() (scripts/kill-orchestrator.js) as pre-approved by the Security Auditor. The guard `if (!path.resolve(planDir).startsWith(WORKSPACE_ROOT)) continue;` constrains lock-file cleanup to paths inside the workspace root. All legitimate log entries have planDir within WORKSPACE_ROOT so there is no behavioral change for normal usage.

Architecture: SIGTERM + 3s wait + SIGKILL escalation is correct; process.kill(pid, 0) liveness check is the right idiom; readline y/N prompt handles TTY/non-TTY correctly; Windows early-return path is clean. Zero external dependencies, full cross-platform path handling.

comments.note: scripts/kill-orchestrator.js findRecentPlanDirs(): applied the defence-in-depth path traversal guard recommended by the Security Auditor. Added `if (!path.resolve(planDir).startsWith(WORKSPACE_ROOT)) continue;` before `planDirs.add(planDir)`. For all legitimate orchestrator log entries, planDir is always within WORKSPACE_ROOT, so this guard has zero behavioral impact on normal usage. It prevents a crafted JSONL entry (plan: '/etc/something') from causing cleanupStaleLocks() to attempt deletion of paths outside the workspace.

scripts/kill-orchestrator.js killProcess(): the 3-second SIGTERM wait is a magic number. A one-line const SIGTERM_GRACE_MS = 3000 at the top of the file would make it self-documenting. Low priority — the intent is clear from the comment, and changing it is out of WP scope.
